q: Electricity supplied to the house is a single-phase form of alternating current (AC).
e: True. Current is charge passing a point each second, and it needs a closed path. Electricity supplied to the house is a single-phase form of alternating current (AC).

q: One of the wires entering a house is the live wire (L) and the other is the neutral wire (N).
e: True. Neutral is held near zero by the supply company and completes the loop. The live wire (L) and the other is the neutral wire (N).

q: The live wire (L) is usually at zero volt while the neutral wire (N) carries a high voltage.
e: False. The right claim is this: The live wire (L) is a dangerous wire as it carries a high voltage while the neutral wire (N) is usually at zero volt. Voltage is potential difference, energy per unit charge between two points. The printed line wrongly says the live wire (L) is usually at zero volt while the neutral wire (N) carries a high voltage.

q: The electricity is fed into the house through the main fuse, meter, main switch and then to the distribution box.
e: True. A fuse is a thin tin-lead wire that melts on overload and opens the circuit on purpose. The main fuse, meter, main switch and then to the distribution box.

q: From the distribution box there are normally three circuits: the lighting circuit, the power circuit (ring main circuit) and heating circuit.
e: True. A ring main feeds sockets both ways around a loop so cable current is shared. The lighting circuit, the power circuit (ring main circuit) and heating circuit.

q: Three cables are colour coded with blue for live (L), brown for neutral (N), and striped green-yellow for earth (E).
e: False. The right claim is this: Three cables are colour coded with brown for live, blue for neutral, striped green-yellow for earth. The printed line wrongly says three cables are colour coded with blue for live (L), brown for neutral (N), and striped green-yellow for earth (E).

q: The old colour code for wiring is red for live, black for neutral and green for earth.
e: True. This old colour code for wiring is red for live, black for neutral and green for earth. Wiring is red for live, black for neutral and green for earth.

q: In the lighting circuit, the light bulbs are arranged in parallel across the mains line.
e: True. The bulb filament is tungsten because it can sit near 3000 °C without melting. Circuit, the light bulbs are arranged in parallel across the mains line.

q: The lighting circuit differs from the other two in that there are three wires: live, neutral, and earth.
e: False. The right claim is this: All electrical appliances require two wires, the live and neutral wires to form a complete circuit. Neutral is held near zero by the supply company and completes the loop. The printed line wrongly says the lighting circuit differs from the other two in that there are three wires: live, neutral, and earth.

q: A lighting circuit must be connected sequentially as live wire, fuse, switch, load and then to neutral wire.
e: True. The live conductor swings plus and minus and is the dangerous one. Sequentially as live wire, fuse, switch, load and then to neutral wire.

q: A power circuit is an electrical system in which distribution points are connected to the main supply in a continuous closed circuit.
e: True. A ring main feeds sockets both ways around a loop so cable current is shared. Points are connected to the main supply in a continuous closed circuit.

q: In a ring main circuit the live, neutral and earth wires form a loop of cable going from the consumer unit to all of the sockets in turn and then back to the consumer unit.
e: True. Earth bonding dumps a fault current so the case cannot stay live. Of the sockets in turn and then back to the consumer unit.

q: Power circuit is for the use of electric cookers, ovens, and washing machines.
e: False. The right claim is this: Heating circuit is for the utilization of appliances such as electric cookers, ovens, hot plates, washing machines and dryers. The printed line wrongly says power circuit is for the use of electric cookers, ovens, and washing machines.

q: Since the current can flow to any particular socket by two ways in a ring main circuit, thinner wires can be used in the whole ring.
e: True. Current is charge passing a point each second, and it needs a closed path. Ring main circuit, thinner wires can be used in the whole ring.

q: Each main ring circuit uses a 30 A fuse.
e: True. A fuse is a thin tin-lead wire that melts on overload and opens the circuit on purpose. The value 30 A is the figure this statement is using.

q: Heating circuit is for the utilization of appliances such as electric cookers, ovens, hot plates, washing machines and dryers.
e: True. Heating circuit is for the utilization of appliances such as electric cookers, ovens, hot plates, washing machines and dryers. Appliances such as electric cookers, ovens, hot plates, washing machines and dryers.

q: The fuse of each circuit must be connected in the neutral (N) lead to protect the appliances.
e: False. The right claim is this: The fuse of each circuit must be connected in the live lead and must never be in the neutral lead. A fuse is a thin tin-lead wire that melts on overload and opens the circuit on purpose. The printed line wrongly says the fuse of each circuit must be connected in the neutral (N) lead to protect the appliances.

q: A circuit breaker is an automatic switch which trips when the current rises above the specified value.
e: True. A breaker is a reusable automatic switch that trips on overload or a short. Automatic switch which trips when the current rises above the specified value.

q: Earthing of an electrical appliance is the most important safety precaution.
e: True. Earth bonding dumps a fault current so the case cannot stay live. Earthing of an electrical appliance is the most important safety precaution.

q: In any electrical appliance the earth wire is always connected to the metal case.
e: True. Earth bonding dumps a fault current so the case cannot stay live. In any electrical appliance the earth wire is always connected to the metal case.
